official.deadline_note: The call opens on 15 January 2027 and closes on 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET, for a fellowship running September to January of the 2027-2028 academic year.
official.application_cycle: Academic year 2027-2028: call opens 15 January 2027, closes 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET, fellowship September to January
official.status_note: The NIAS page currently shows 'Application Closed'. The next call, for the academic year 2027-2028, opens on 15 January 2027 and closes on 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET.
benefits: Five months of funded research time at NIAS in Amsterdam, from September to January
A personal stipend paid directly to the fellow, or a Dutch University Grant paid to the home institution for scholars affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute
An office and research facilities at NIAS, plus full use of the KB's collections, facilities, services and expertise
Subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam where eligible, or reimbursement of local public transport
Membership of an international community of scholars, writers and artists, and participation in the academic, community and outreach programme
eligibility: Scholars with at least three years of research experience after obtaining their PhD, measured on the closing date of the call; institutional affiliation is not required
Creative practitioners with at least three years of independent practice since graduating, or equivalent experience; affiliation is not required
A project that relates to the KB research agenda or extends its scope, including questions concerning the KB's own collections, digital or otherwise
Proposals taking an international or comparative perspective are especially welcome
Able to be at NIAS four days a week for the whole semester, since a fellowship is a full-time commitment
An excellent command of spoken and written English, the working language at NIAS
requirements: Submit the application through the online application form
Provide a project proposal of no more than 1,500 words, including footnotes and excluding references
Provide an academic or artistic CV of no more than four pages, including international collaborations and a list of key publications, preferably recent and in refereed journals or books
Provide a statement of no more than 300 words explaining how the project relates to your work so far and why the fellowship comes at the right time
Be present at NIAS four days a week from the start to the end of the semester
Publish any resulting publications under the Creative Commons CC BY 4.0 licence
documents: Project proposal of no more than 1,500 words including footnotes, excluding references
Academic or artistic CV of no more than four pages with international collaborations and key publications
Statement of no more than 300 words on fit with your work and timing
selection_criteria: Quality and originality of the proposal
The candidate's scholarly or artistic achievements so far
What the candidate expects from the NIAS community and will contribute to it
Significance of the project for the policies and practices of the KB or of libraries in general, or for the place of the library in a liberal democracy
Preference is given to proposals that bring new questions or unexpected dimensions to the KB research agenda
coverage: Personal stipend paid directly to the fellow
Dutch University Grant paid to the home institution for scholars affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute
Office and research facilities at NIAS
Subsidised accommodation in Amsterdam where eligible, or reimbursement of local public transport
No tuition, travel or workshop costs are published; NIAS does not provide studios, materials or tools for artistic work
application_method: Wait for the call to open on 15 January 2027
Upload the project proposal, the CV and the statement, each within its word or page limit
Submit before 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET
official.application_route: Complete the NIAS online application form and upload a project proposal within 1,500 words, a four-page CV and a 300-word statement, before the call closes on 15 March 2027 at noon CET.
official.study_mode: Full-time residency at NIAS, four days a week for the whole semester
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or residency restriction is published; applicants may be based in the Netherlands or abroad, with or without institutional affiliation
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants internationally; institutional affiliation is not required
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all scholarly and artistic disciplines, but the project must relate to the KB research agenda or extend its scope, for example the future of the public library or the library as a public institution and pillar of liberal democracy
official.research_requirement: A project proposal of no more than 1,500 words is required; artists may propose artistic production as a research strategy or research ahead of production, although NIAS provides no studios, materials or tools
official.duration: Five months, from September to January, one fellowship per academic year
official.description: The KB Fellowship at NIAS offers researchers and creative practitioners five months to work on the future of the public library, or on the library as a public institution and a pillar of liberal democracy. Established by NIAS and the KB, the National Library of the Netherlands, in 2025, it continues an earlier KB Fellowship that ran from 2004 to 2018.
official.program_type: Fellowship at a national advanced study institute, funded jointly by NIAS and the National Library of the Netherlands
official.english_requirement: Applicants should speak and write English well enough to take a full part in the life of the institute and to benefit from the responses of their peers; a test or interview may form part of the selection procedure

verification.notes: Benefits, eligibility, word limits, application parts, ranking criteria and the 2027-2028 call dates were read directly from the NIAS KB Fellowship page. The project proposal limit is 1,500 words including footnotes and excluding references, as stated on the page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fellowship for a finished or nearly finished project, not a grant to start one: the 300-word statement asking why the fellowship comes at the right time is a genuine filter, and reviewers will read it as evidence that you have the material and the time to use five months well. Because eligibility is measured on the closing date of the call, the three years of post-PhD or post-graduation experience must be complete by 15 March 2027, not by the start of the fellowship. Note that the KB itself ranks candidates first and NIAS decides second, so the proposal has to satisfy a library-and-collections agenda as much as your own discipline's standards.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career scholars or creative practitioners at least three years past their PhD or graduation, working on libraries, archives, public knowledge or democratic access to information, who can spend four days a week in Amsterdam from September to January.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the KB research agenda page before drafting, since the ranking committee gives preference to proposals that bring new questions or unexpected dimensions to it
Trim the proposal to 1,500 words including footnotes and excluding references, and keep the CV to four pages with recent refereed work listed
Write the 300-word statement last, once the proposal shows clearly what remains unfinished and why five months of protected time changes what you can deliver
Confirm your funding route with your institution in advance if you are Dutch-affiliated, since the Dutch University Grant is paid to the institution rather than to you
Check early that you can be in Amsterdam four days a week for the whole semester, including travel around your teaching or clinical commitments
common_rejection_risks: Exceeding the 1,500-word proposal limit or the four-page CV limit, which are stated hard bounds

Proposing a project that only touches the KB agenda in passing, when the KB-appointed committee ranks on significance for the KB, for libraries generally, or for the library's place in liberal democracy
Counting research experience that is not complete by the closing date of the call
Assuming a studio, materials or tools are provided for artistic work, when NIAS explicitly does not supply them
Treating the fellowship as part-time, when NIAS requires four days a week presence for the whole semester
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights to Amsterdam, most living costs and any artistic production costs are not covered; the stipend is a living-cost contribution and accommodation is only subsidised where eligible, with local public transport reimbursement as the fallback.
document_audit: The CV must list international collaborations and key publications, preferably recent and in refereed journals or books, so an outdated list signals drift
The statement and the proposal serve different purposes: the proposal is the project, the statement is the case for timing and fit with your own work
References and bibliographies are excluded from the word count, but footnotes are included, so use footnotes sparingly
If your outputs would be published anyway, check that CC BY 4.0 is acceptable to your publisher and co-authors before you accept any award
The application is a single online form with uploads, so no covering letter or email materials will reach the committee
alerts: The call window is only two months, 15 January to 15 March, with a hard noon CET cut-off on the final day
Only one fellowship is awarded per academic year, so the cohort is small and the competition pool is broad across all disciplines
The Fellowship Advisory Committee deliberately balances the cohort by discipline, location, career stage and gender, so an outstanding application can still lose on cohort fit
NIAS also runs a separate general NIAS Fellowship and Theme Group Fellowships, and you should check whether your project suits one of those instead
The funding route differs by affiliation, so confirm with NIAS whether your situation yields a personal stipend or a University Grant to your institution
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online form with three uploads before the 15 March 2027 noon CET close, then an eligibility check by NIAS, a ranking by a KB-appointed committee, and a final decision by the NIAS Director on the advice of the Fellowship Advisory Committee.
